rewritten_query: what is n8n workflow automation tool and how does it work
final_answer:
### What is n8n?

n8n (pronounced “n-eight-n”) is a low-code, open-source workflow automation platform built with Node.js [1, 2]. It is designed to allow users to orchestrate logic, connect various services, and scale pipelines with minimal boilerplate [1]. 

The tool is characterized by its flexibility, offering a balance between the simplicity of no-code visual interfaces and the power of custom coding [3]. It can be self-hosted on a user's own server—which is particularly beneficial for industries requiring high data privacy—or used via cloud-hosted setups [2, 3, 4].

### How n8n Works

n8n operates on a node-based architecture, where workflows are constructed visually in a browser-based interface [4]. 

#### Workflow Structure
An n8n workflow is an automated sequence of tasks consisting of multiple nodes [2]. These nodes represent individual steps or actions, such as sending an email, scraping a website, transforming data, or connecting to an API [4]. A typical workflow includes:

*   **Trigger Nodes:** These initiate the workflow based on specific events, such as a webhook or a time-based trigger [2, 4].
*   **Action Nodes:** These perform specific tasks, such as querying databases, sending messages, or calling APIs [4].
*   **Logic Nodes:** These are used to control the path of the workflow by adding conditions, loops, or custom code [4].

#### Customization and Integration
While n8n is a visual, no-code tool, it is also developer-friendly [2, 3]. Users can:
*   **Integrate Services:** It supports over 400 integrations out of the box, including tools like Slack, Google Sheets, GitHub, AWS, and OpenAI [3, 4].
*   **Add Custom Logic:** Users can incorporate JavaScript or Python functions directly into their workflows [2, 3].
*   **Extend Functionality:** It allows for the import of libraries from the Node package manager (npm) or Python, and users can connect to any API even if a prebuilt node does not exist [2, 3].

### Use Cases
n8n is used to automate a wide range of tasks, including:
*   **AI-Driven Automations:** Extracting data, processing it, sending it to an LLM, and presenting the results [1].
*   **Marketing:** Capturing form responses and automating email follow-ups [4].
*   **Finance:** Updating financial spreadsheets with daily exchange rates [4].
*   **E-commerce:** Synchronizing inventory across platforms following a sale [4].
*   **Development:** Monitoring GitHub commits to trigger CI/CD pipelines [4].

### Sources

[2] https://www.codecademy.com/article/build-ai-workflows-with-n8n
[3] https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/a-beginners-guide-to-automation-with-n8n
[4] https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/what-n8n-beginners-guide-workflow-automation-tool-sandaruwan-upfic

As a self-hostable, open-source automation platform, n8n lets you orchestrate logic, connect services, and scale pipelines with minimal boilerplate. search_results.content: # A Beginner’s Guide to Automation with n8n. Whether it’s moving data between apps, triggering actions when something changes, or building smart systems that run on their own, automation can save hours every week. The problem is that most automation platforms make you choose between flexibility and simplicity. Writing your own scripts in Python or JavaScript gives you full control but takes more time to build and maintain. It is an open-source workflow automation platform that provides both control and simplicity. You can drag and connect nodes to create workflows or write code when needed. In this article, we’ll learn how to build and deploy your own automation workflows using n8n. By the end, you’ll have a working automation server and the knowledge to create smart, self-running workflows for any use case. This large library of ready-to-use nodes means you can connect most tools you use every day without needing to write any code at all.
